## 1. Identity & classification
- **ID:** 16029205689 · cloned from **22021505280 → 16028605475 → 16029205689**.
- **Title:** [WCL][DPMO] PMC Stuck at Phase3Bootflow, waiting for IP_ready assertion from UFS Controller
- **Program / release:** WCL A0 (`package.wclc-n204-a0`) · also confirmed on **A1**.
- **Component:** `hw.ufs` · **Owner:** msure · **Submitted:** 2025-11-19 · **Status:** complete · **Conclusion:** hw.bug · classification **Intel Top Secret**.
- **Signature tag:** `ufs-fusepull-cdc-race-on-boot` (boot-time PGCB/CDC fuse-pull class).
- **IP / layer:** UFS fuse-pull via **IOSF2OCP bridge** + **PGCB sub-IP** (clock/reset) instantiated in UFS ↔ PMC PGCB ↔ Fuse Controller.
- **Scope:** one bug across a **clone chain of 3 sightings** + Bugeco + PMC-FW WA (see §10). **Distinct from `ufs-fabric-timeout-on-pkgc` (16027585017)** — that is runtime PKGC fabric-timeout; this is **boot-time fuse-pull CDC**.

## 2. Symptom (observable) + reproducibility profile
- During **warm-reset (WR) cycling** (DPMO/QS reliability), the **PMC hangs at Phase-3 bootflow (`PC:0005`)** polling for **`ufs_ip_ready_status`**, which the UFS controller never asserts → boot never completes.
- **At the hang:** PMC SRAM trace prints **only "WDT timer expired"**; **no MCA**, **no global/host-partition reset**, cores **inactive/sleep**; PKGC = `PKGC_IDLE_ON_C0`.
- **UFS state:** power well + controller IP power **up**, UFS **PHY** IP_ready asserted, but UFS **controller** IP_ready **not** asserted `[confirmed]`.
- **Reproducibility:** **sporadic — ~1 in 1000+ cycles** (a few thousand). Timing-dependent race → a **Heisenbug**: enabling **IOSF SB trace** or arming VISA makes it stop reproducing (observability perturbs the timing).
- **Config dependence:** repro'd on **3★ (UFS-enabled)** config; the 4★/5★ (NVMe, UFS-disabled) configs also hung until unblocked — see §7 "why WCL only".

## 3. Initial triage — first discriminators
- **First signal:** PMC stuck looping Phase-3 bootflow at **`PC:0005`** with **WDT-expired only**, no MCA, no reset → not a data-path or MCA fault; it's a **boot init / IP-handshake** stall.
- **Fastest confirm:** read the **fuse-pull FSM** — it is stuck in **`fuse_pull_ready (001)`**, never reaching **`fuse_pull_done (006)`**; and the **IOSF2OCP bridge FSM** is stuck in **"Fuse Pull Request"** while the **fuse-puller FSM is Idle**.
- **Rule-in (it IS this):** PMC at `PC:0005` waiting `ufs_ip_ready_status`; fuse-pull stuck at `001` (not `006`); Fuse-Controller history shows **`ufs_pga` request served but IOSF2OCP-bridge request NOT received**; WDT-only, no MCA/reset; sporadic on WR cycling.
- **Rule-out (it is NOT this):** any `IS_` **SBFES/HCFES** fatal / OCP fabric timeout / 804µs `int_sts` hang / DPC-watchdog BSOD → that's the **runtime** `ufs-fabric-timeout-on-pkgc` class (16027585017), not this boot-time fuse-pull bug. **Caution — do NOT rule this out just because UFS is "disabled":** WCL's strap/BIOS-disabled **4★/5★** configs still run the boot-time fuse-pull and **do** hit it; only parts that **fully SMIP-static-disable UFS so the fuse-pull path never runs** (PTL/LNL) are immune.
- **Nearest look-alikes:** 16027585017 (same WCL UFS↔PMC, same owner, "UFS unresponsive") — deciding tell: **boot Phase-3 fuse-pull FSM stuck** vs **runtime `IS_` fabric timeout**. Prior-art **1406831804** = same PGCB/CDC class, different IP instance.

- **Expect:** ~1-in-1000+ WR cycles → hang at `PC:0005`.

## 6. Debug flow (diagnostic narrowing)
Logic-ordered (not chronological) — how the fault was narrowed. Evidence rows → §5. Repro logistics,
WA rollout, and validation cycles are NOT here (→ §8 fix / §10 linkage).
1. **Symptom:** WR cycling → PMC stuck Phase-3 (`PC:0005`) waiting UFS IP_ready; no MCA, cores idle, no reset → PMC blocked on a single IP-ready. (§5a-1,3)
2. **Rule out config artifact:** 4★/5★ (NVMe, UFS strap-disabled) hang **identically** to 3★ (UFS-enabled) → the fuse-pull sequence runs even when UFS is strap-disabled → not a UFS-*workload* bug; it lives in the fuse/reset path.
3. **Localize the block:** `ufsx2_ip_ready_sts=0` while `ufspw1_ip_ready_sts=1` (controller not ready, PHY ready); fuse-pull stuck `001`≠`006`; **no fuse *errors*** (`fuse_strap_cpl_status=0x0`) and only **partial** fuse state in bridge regs (`fuse1=0x001c1000`, `fuse2/3=0`) — but the fuse-pull **did not complete** (bridge request never received, §5c), so `ufs_ip_ready` never asserts. The pull is **incomplete**, not merely a missing 'done' bit. (§5a-5,6,8,9)
4. **Classify as timing race:** arming IOSF-SB trace / VISA makes it **vanish** (thousands of clean cycles) → perturbation-sensitive → race, not a functional bug; the **~26 µs** IP_Request→IP_Ready window is the arena. (§5f trap)
5. **Freeze the FSMs:** scandump → fuse-puller FSM **Idle**, bridge FSM stuck **"Fuse Pull Request"**; StatusScope → **2 IOSF2OCP FSMs illegal** → bridge wedged mid-request. (§5b, §5d)
6. **Pin the lost request:** Fuse Controller history → **`ufs_pga` served, iosf2ocp-bridge request never received** → the request was dropped before the controller ever saw it. (§5c)
7. **Mechanism:** Fuse-Puller RTL transition qualified by **`fscan_mode`** → a glitch drops the request → **PGCB/CDC metastability race** (reset-deassert edge async to the PGCB clock). Full root cause → §7. (§5e)

## 7. Root cause (precise mechanism + class)
- **Class:** **design-rtl** — a **PGCB / clock-domain-crossing (CDC) race** in the PGCB sub-IP instantiated in UFS (pre-**2017** PGCB version; same class as prior HSD **1406831804**). **RTL disposition: `[confirmed]` REJECTED** (`rejected.future_product`, `bug_class=hw_rtl`) — no silicon/RTL fix; permanently mitigated in **PMC FW** (ticket `16029333243`, `ccb_workaround=fw.pmc`).
- **Mechanism (converged, CCB WW49.2 → confirmed WW51):** on **IP-wake assertion** two events fire **unsynchronized**:
  1. PMC **PGCB** state machine recognizes the IP power-up transition and **de-asserts the SB (sideband) reset**.
  2. The **PGCB state machine in UFS** exits **WARMRST**, forcing the SB-logic clock on with the **PGCB clock**.
  The **reset-de-assertion edge is asynchronous to the PGCB clock** → **metastability** in sequential logic → the fuse-puller's request is lost. Result: **IOSF2OCP-bridge fuse request never sent from the UFS IP** → **fuse-pull stuck `001`** → UFS controller **IP_ready never asserts** → PMC waits forever at Phase-3 → hang.
- **Two competing hypotheses investigated — how they were adjudicated** `[confirmed: WCL UFS IP_READY Issue.pptx]`:
  1. **`fscan_mode` glitch (DFT signal):** IP-Val simulation that deliberately glitched `fscan_mode` **reproduced the same FSM behavior as the scan dump** — a real, sim-corroborated mechanism for losing the request. **However**, DFX-team review of the scan logic concluded a `fscan_mode` glitch is **"very unlikely in Functional mode"** — `fscan_mode` is a DFT/scan-control signal not expected to toggle during normal functional operation. Net: explains the *symptom* under fault-injection, but is **not the accepted field mechanism**.
  2. **PGCB/CDC async reset-deassertion (accepted):** preliminary analysis of FC waveforms showed the **pre-2017 PGCB/CDC async-reset-on-WARMRST-exit** issue present in this instance. This is the mechanism the CCB ultimately adopted — confirmed by the fix itself: **Solution 2 (a pure ~20 µs timing guard band, no `fscan_mode`/`ip_ready` logic change) alone eliminates the failure**, which only makes sense if the async reset edge — not a `fscan_mode` glitch — is the true root cause.
  - **A parallel, ruled-out-by-omission theory:** voltage droop (Vnn/VnnAon) across repeated WR cycles was also suspected and investigated; it does not reappear in the CCB's final root-cause conclusion — treat as **considered, not confirmed**.
- **Timing:** IP_Request→IP_Ready must complete within **~26 µs**; the race misses it once in a few-thousand cycles.
- **Why WCL only** `[confirmed]`: **PTL & LNL static-disable UFS** so they never run this fuse-pull; **WCL does not static-disable UFS** (brings UFS up at boot then power-gates the PHY to save ~12 mW WC), so only WCL exercises the path that trips the CDC race.
- **Scope beyond WCL** `[confirmed: HSD 16029333243 CCB AR, WW51.4]`: **NVL IS impacted** (same pre-2017 PGCB/CDC version) — disposition **TBD**, tracked in the NVL bugboard separately. Cross-checked: **no other WCL IP** carries the 2016/pre-2017 PGCB/CDC version — impact confirmed **UFS-only within WCL**.
- **Residual/related risk (not yet fixed):** `[confirmed: WCL UFS IP_READY Issue ww51.4.pptx, updated WW52.4]` UFS has a **second instance of the same PGCB/CDC sub-IP inside the PHY SIP** — the IP team confirms **the same defect is present there too**, though it has **not manifested/failed in testing so far**. The IP team recommends applying the **same fix opportunistically**; CCB directs a **separate HSD be filed to PMC** to track it (not covered by this ticket's fix).

### 7b. Fingerprint registers (high level)
- **`ufs_ip_ready_status`** — the bit PMC polls at Phase-3; **never set** in this failure.
- **fuse-pull FSM** — stuck **`fuse_pull_ready (001)`**, not **`fuse_pull_done (006)`**; **IOSF2OCP bridge FSM** stuck **"Fuse Pull Request"**, fuse-puller FSM **Idle**.
- **`UFS_FUSE_REG1`** — Solution-1 WA wrote **`0x3800`** (derives UFS Device ID); **superseded** — Solution 2 (shipping) does not touch this register (see §8).
- **`SB_PMA_FSM_STATE`** = `SB_FSM_FUSE_PUSH_DONE`; **`pmc_arc_pc`** stuck `0xb0548` / `PC:0005`.
- Full decode/definitions → `reference/ufs-glossary.md` (PGCB, CDC, WARMRST, IOSF2OCP, fuse-puller, fscan_mode).

## 8. Fix & verification (workaround + status)
- **RTL disposition:** `[confirmed]` **REJECTED** (`rejected.future_product`) — no RTL/silicon fix for this stepping; mitigation is **permanent** via PMC FW (`WA validity: permanent`, ticket `16029333243`).
- **WA v2 — FAILED:** ignore `ufs_ip_ready_status` in PMC FW, but it **missed the PM Dashboard list** entry → still repro'd.
- **Solution 1 / WA v3 — interim (superseded, see below):** `PMC_WCL_N_A0_2100.76.00.7023_Engineering_RemoveUFSIpReadyStatusCheck_v3_prod`:
  - Dashboard change so **PMC ignores `UFS IP_Ready_STS`**.
  - **PMC writes `0x3800` to `UFS_FUSE_REG1`** (device-ID) for matching PCIe endpoint.
  - **Verification:** not reproducible on **A0 & A1**; ~2000 cycles on 8 CVE setups + SIV mass-validation clean (table below). **Released by WW50.2 to intercept RC1 QS `[done]`.** Tracked in **PMC-FW WA 18044008985**.

  **SIV validation with PMC-FW v3 patch** (`...RemoveUFSIpReadyStatusCheck_v3_prod`):
```
| Config          | Cycle | Result                     |
| 5★ (NVMe)       | WR    | 12K (1500×9 DUTs) — non-repro |
| 5★ (NVMe)       | CS    | 5K — not observed          |
| 5★ (NVMe)       | S4    | 6K — not observed          |
| 4★ (NVMe)       | WR    | 12K (1500×9) — non-repro   |
| 4★ (NVMe)       | CS    | 2K — not observed          |
| 4★ (NVMe)       | S4    | 5K — not observed          |
| 3★ (UFS)        | WR    | 5K A1 + 5K A0 — non-repro  |
| 3★ (UFS)        | CS    | 2.5K A0 — non-repro        |
```
- **Solution 2 (root-cause WA, shipping) — CONFIRMED, supersedes Solution 1:** `[confirmed: HSD 16029333243, WW51 bugboard]` PMC FW adds a **~20 µs / 50 PGCB-cycle guard band** between "IP wake" and "side-reset de-assertion" (32 clock-on + 3 switch + 10+ guard) so the reset edge is clear of the PGCB clock.
  - **Confirmed working — no failures observed in post-Si testing.** `[confirmed: HSD 16029333243 WW51 bugboard + WCL UFS IP_READY Issue ww51.4.pptx]` "Runs are OK; no repro." Bug is root-caused and the workaround is working.
  - **Supersedes Solution 1:** the **`ip_ready`-ignore logic was REMOVED** in Solution 2 — **only the 20 µs delay remains** in the PMC-FW patch. A new PCR was raised to formally capture removal of the Solution-1 `ip_ready` bypass (superseding `18044008985`).
  - **Schedule:** **released on WW52.2** to intercept RC2 QS (updated from the earlier WW51.2 estimate; CCB tracked this WW51→WW52.2 slip explicitly). **PRQ in WW09.** Detail PPT: `WCL UFS IP_READY Issue.pptx` (root-cause investigation) / Bugeco **16029333243**.
  - **CCB final decision:** reject the RTL HSD; approve the Solution-2 PMC-FW workaround as **permanent**.
- **Follow-up (from investigation, not yet in final CCB conclusion):** voltage droop (Vnn/VnnAon) across WR cycles was checked as a parallel hypothesis; superseded once Solution 2 (pure timing fix) confirmed working — **not the root cause**, but retained as a monitoring item.
- **Open AR (low priority):** file a **separate tracking HSD** for the second PGCB/CDC instance in the **UFS PHY SIP** (not covered by this fix).

## 9. Retrospective (avoidable? prevention? detection gap?)
- **Avoidable:** a **known PGCB/CDC class** (prior HSD 1406831804) re-instantiated in UFS without the guard band — a CDC-review checklist for reset-vs-clock synchronization on IP-wake would likely have caught it.
- **Prevention:** add the **~20 µs guard band** in RTL/PMC-FW by design; add a **fuse-pull-completion + IP_ready timeout** validation to the UFS boot/WR-cycling suite; default-on **scandump on Phase-3 stall**.
- **Detection gap:** **sporadic (~1/1000+)** and **Heisenbug** — SB-trace/VISA mask it, so it needs **high-volume WR cycling** + **scandump** to catch; easy to miss in short runs. A **second instance of the same PGCB/CDC sub-IP in the UFS PHY SIP** carries the **same defect** but has **not manifested/failed in any testing so far** — an open, unfixed detection gap; IP recommends an opportunistic fix, tracked via a separate HSD to PMC.
- **Dead-ends / false leads:**
  - **Ignoring `ufs_ip_ready` in PMC FW v2** — didn't work (missed the **PM Dashboard list**); the tell was PMC still waiting despite the "ignore".
  - **SMIP static-disable WA** — only helps **NVMe (UFS-disabled)** configs, not the 3★ UFS config; the v3 ignore-WA works for both.
  - **Arming IOSF-SB-trace / VISA to catch it** — masked the race (no repro with observability on) — wasted cycles until scandump-after-hang was adopted.
  - **Early "4★ vs 3★ same bug?" doubt** — 4★ is non-UFS; resolved by confirming BIOS/strap disable and that both stall in the same fuse-pull flow.

## 12. Debug story (conversational narrative for first-time readers)

**Where it starts — a rare boot hang under stress.** You're running warm-reset reliability cycling on
WCL (DPMO/QS). Almost always fine — but roughly **once in a few thousand cycles**, the box just stops
during boot. The PMC is stuck at **Phase-3 bootflow, `PC:0005`**, endlessly polling a bit called
**`ufs_ip_ready_status`** that never turns on. No blue screen, no MCA, no reset — the PMC's own trace
only says **"watchdog timer expired."** The cores are asleep. It's a quiet, stubborn hang.

**First look — who's not answering?** The UFS power well is up, the controller IP has power
(`ufsx2_pwr_sts=1`), and even the UFS **PHY** reports ready (`ufspw1_ip_ready_sts=1`) — but the UFS
**controller** never raises its bit (`ufsx2_ip_ready_sts=0`). A clean split: PHY ready, controller not.
Why? On this SoC the controller only asserts IP_ready once four things are true: IP powered, clocks on,
no fuse errors, and — the key one — **fuse-pull done**. Read the fuse-pull state machine and there's
your smell: it's frozen at **`fuse_pull_ready (001)`** and never advances to **`fuse_pull_done (006)`**.
And here's the paradox that misleads everyone at first: the fuse-completion status is **clean**
(`fuse_strap_cpl_status = 0x0`, no error) and one bridge fuse register even holds a value
(`fuse1 = 0x001c1000`) — so it *looks* like the fuses arrived. They didn't, not fully: `fuse2/3` are
still `0`, and the Fuse Controller never even received the bridge's pull request. The pull **started
and was lost mid-flight** — the *done* never fires because the pull genuinely never finished.

**A red herring — is it even a UFS bug?** Early on the picture is muddy: the hang also shows up on the
**4★ and 5★ configs**, which are **NVMe (UFS disabled)**. So is this really UFS at all? The team
confirms BIOS and straps do disable the UFS controller there — and yet the box still wedges in the
**same fuse-pull flow**. That's the tell: the fuse-pull sequence runs at boot **regardless** of whether
UFS is the storage device. This isn't a UFS-*workload* bug; it lives in the fuse/reset plumbing that UFS
sits behind. That realization pulls everyone off "storage" and onto "boot-time fuse pull."

**The frustrating part — it hides when you watch it.** The obvious move is to arm traces and catch it
in the act. So the team enables **IOSF sideband tracing** — and the bug **vanishes** (3000 clean
cycles). Same story with VISA. This is a classic **Heisenbug**: it's a *timing* race, and the act of
observing it changes the timing just enough to dodge it. The only reliable evidence comes from
**scan-dumping the machine after it's already hung.**

**The scan dump tells the truth.** In the dump, the **fuse-puller FSM is sitting Idle**, while the
**IOSF2OCP bridge FSM is stuck in "Fuse Pull Request."** And the Fuse Controller keeps a log of its
last 15 requests — in it, the other client (`ufs_pga`) got served fine, but the **bridge's fuse request
was never even received.** So the bridge *thinks* it asked for a fuse pull, but the request never made
it out. The handshake is broken at birth. **StatusScope agrees from another angle**: two of the
IOSF2OCP FSMs are parked in states that are **electrically impossible** in normal operation — the
bridge is genuinely wedged, not merely slow. And the whole handshake is meant to finish inside a
**~26 µs** window from IP_Request to IP_Ready; miss that window once, and the bridge never recovers.

**The "aha" — a clock/reset race.** When the IP wakes, two things happen at once, on two different
clocks, with nobody synchronizing them: the **PMC's PGCB** de-asserts the sideband reset, while the
**UFS's PGCB** exits WARMRST and slams the sideband clock on. Because the reset-release edge is
**asynchronous to the PGCB clock**, every so often it lands in the danger zone and causes
**metastability** in the logic, and the fuse-puller's request is lost. (Early on, the team also caught
this by deliberately glitching `fscan_mode` — the puller's transition qualifier — in simulation, which
reproduced the exact same stuck-FSM behavior as the scan dump. But a DFX review of the scan logic
concluded a real `fscan_mode` glitch is very unlikely in **functional** silicon, so that was a
symptom-matching lead, not the final answer.) The confirmed culprit is the CDC race itself — proven by
the fix: a **pure timing delay**, with no `fscan_mode` or IP_ready logic involved, makes the bug vanish.
It's the same **PGCB/CDC** gremlin seen before (HSD 1406831804, pre-2017 vintage), just re-instantiated
inside UFS. And it only bites **WCL**, because PTL and LNL simply switch UFS off — WCL keeps UFS alive
at boot (to save ~12 mW) and then power-gates it, so only WCL ever runs this fuse pull.

**The fix — buy time, then remove the race for good.** The clean fix is in silicon, but QS can't wait.
So the first move is PMC firmware: **stop caring about UFS IP_ready** and just **write the expected
device ID (`0x3800`) into `UFS_FUSE_REG1`** yourself. The first attempt (v2) embarrassingly still hung
— it forgot to also drop IP_ready from the PMC **dashboard list** — but **v3** got it right and the bug
went away across A0 and A1: **12K warm-reset cycles per config, plus 5–6K each of connected-standby and
S4**, all clean. That's the stopgap (Solution 1). The **real cure (Solution 2)** gives the reset edge
room to breathe: a **~20 µs guard band** (50 PGCB cycles) between "IP wake" and "reset de-assert," with
**no `fscan_mode` or IP_ready trickery at all**. It shipped, and post-Si testing came back clean — CCB
called it root-caused and working, then had the **`ip_ready`-ignore hack from Solution 1 stripped back
out**, leaving only the clean 20 µs delay as the permanent fix. The RTL bug itself was formally
**rejected** (no silicon respin) — this timing fix in PMC firmware is the lasting answer.

**If you're debugging this tomorrow — the short version.** WCL, UFS-enabled, warm-reset cycling, box
hangs at `PC:0005` waiting on `ufs_ip_ready_status`. **Don't** arm SB-trace/VISA (it'll hide). Cycle
until it hangs, then **scan-dump** and read the **fuse-pull FSM (stuck 001)** and the **IOSF2OCP bridge
FSM (stuck Fuse-Pull-Request)**. If you see that, you're on this bug — a PGCB/CDC race eating the fuse
request. The **permanent** fix is a PMC-FW ~20 µs reset/clock guard band (no register trickery needed);
the older ignore-IP_ready + `UFS_FUSE_REG1=0x3800` patch was only an interim stopgap and has been retired.

**Honest caveats.** The RTL bug was formally rejected (permanently mitigated in PMC FW, not silicon).
`fscan_mode` glitching was a strong simulation lead but DFX judged it unlikely in functional mode — the
CDC async-reset race is the accepted mechanism. Voltage-droop (Vnn/VnnAon) was checked as a parallel
hypothesis but doesn't appear in the final CCB conclusion. **NVL is confirmed impacted** by the same
pre-2017 PGCB/CDC version (disposition tracked separately in the NVL bugboard); no other WCL IP carries
it. One residual, unfixed item: UFS has a **second instance of this same PGCB/CDC sub-IP inside the PHY
SIP**, confirmed to carry **the same defect** even though it hasn't manifested in any testing yet — IP
recommends fixing it opportunistically, and CCB has directed a separate HSD be filed to PMC to track it.
The raw scandump/StatusScope artifacts still aren't attached here. Ask msure/gdharmes/muralibh to
confirm any remaining detail.
